requirements.text: Create a new service named Cloud Email Platform with description 'Cloud-based enterprise email platform' while keeping all the fields same as the Enterprise Email service
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_049' AND name = 'Cloud Email Platform' AND description = 'Cloud-based enterprise email platform' AND owned_by = 'USER_004' AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND used_for = 'production' AND status = 'operational' AND service_classification = 'business' AND business_criticality = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (SVC_048 is the highest service id in the seed)
owned_by, org_id, used_for, status, service_classification and business_criticality copied from Enterprise Email (SVC_001), since the request keeps all its fields the same
org_id is not tested by the benchmark check; added because it is one of the fields the request keeps the same as SVC_001

requirements.text: made a new corresponding service offering for it named as 'Cloud Email Platform - Standard' with short description as 'Standard cloud mailbox', used for a 'production', status as 'operational', service_classification as 'application' and business_criticality as 'critical'
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id = 'SVCOFF_061' AND name = 'Cloud Email Platform - Standard' AND short_description = 'Standard cloud mailbox' AND business_service = 'SVC_049' AND owned_by = 'USER_004' AND used_for = 'production' AND status = 'operational' AND service_classification = 'application' AND business_criticality = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (SVCOFF_060 is the highest service offering id in the seed)
business_service is the new Cloud Email Platform service, SVC_049, as the offering is 'for it'
owned_by = USER_004 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (it matches the owner of the service it belongs to)
short_description is stated in the request but not tested by the benchmark check

requirements.text: any currently open (new and in_progress) incidents associated with Enterprise Email should be moved to the new service and it's offerings
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id IN ('INC_004', 'INC_073') AND service = 'SVC_049' AND service_offering = 'SVCOFF_061'
requirements.source: Open incidents moved to new service and service offering
assumptions: the selector is every incident in status new or in_progress on SVC_001 or its offerings SVCOFF_001 and SVCOFF_018: INC_004 (new) and INC_073 (in_progress) on the seed
the new service has a single offering, so both incidents take SVCOFF_061, including INC_073, which has no offering on the seed

requirements.text: any currently open (new and in_progress) incidents associated with Enterprise Email
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id IN ('INC_018', 'INC_048', 'INC_075') AND service = 'SVC_001' AND service_offering IN ('SVCOFF_001', 'SVCOFF_018')
assumptions: boundary of the open-incident selector: INC_018, INC_048 and INC_075 are on Enterprise Email but resolved, so the move to the new service leaves them on SVC_001 and its offerings

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_001' AND status = 'retired'
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: a decommissioned, unsupported service is set to retired (update_service is available and retired is a service status in the seed)

requirements.text: The existing Enterprise Email service and its related offerings are no longer supported.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE service_offering_id IN ('SVCOFF_001', 'SVCOFF_018') AND status = 'retired'
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the unsupported offerings are set to retired (update_service_offering is available)
SVCOFF_001 and SVCOFF_018 are the only offerings with business_service = SVC_001 in the seed

notes: The acting user, Karen Watkins (USER_039), is an admin, so every write is permitted. The request never names a status for Enterprise Email or its offerings; retirement is read from 'decommissioned' and 'no longer supported'. The new service keeps SVC_001's operational status, since the copy is taken from the service as it stands before it is retired. The new offering's org_id and description are not fixed by the request (the 'keep all the fields same' clause applies to the service, not the offering), so they are not tested. No on_hold incident is associated with Enterprise Email on the seed. The two independent passes agreed on every requirement, cell, value and disposition; there were no disagreements to resolve.
